chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abdillah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'So remember the name of Allah upon her when she is lined up.' He said: 'That is when you line her up for slaughter; you tie her forelegs between the hock and the knee, and the obligation is that her sides fall to the ground when she lies down on the earth.'

key_terms.النَّحْر: Slaughter (specifically of camels or large animals by severing the throat)
key_terms.الْخُفِّ: The hock joint of the animal's leg
key_terms.صَوَافَّ: Lined up or standing in a row (referring to the animal's position)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct physical positioning and procedure for slaughtering an animal according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific physical posture required for ritual slaughter (dhabh) as alluded to in the Quranic command to 'remember Allah's name upon it.' It establishes that the animal must be lined up (saff) and restrained by tying its legs from the hock to the knee, ensuring it falls squarely on its side (junub) before the cut is made, a detail crucial for validating the act in Shia fiqh.
